headline: Ancient painted tomb uncovered near Egypt's Luxor

sources.title: Archaeologists uncover 3,000-year-old tomb near Egypt's Luxor
3,000-year-old tomb of ancient Egyptian official Paser discovered in Luxor's Theban Necropolis
3,000-year-old Egyptian tomb with vivid afterlife paintings uncovered near Luxor

chunks.text: Archaeologists in Egypt have {{dug up}} an [[ancient]] [[tomb]] near the city of Luxor. A Dutch team from Leiden University {{teamed up with}} Egypt's [[antiquities]] authority to [[explore]] the west bank of the Nile. The tomb is about 3,000 years old, and it [[belonged to]] an official named Paser. Experts believe it {{dates back}} to the Ramesside period, a great age of Egyptian [[pharaohs]].

chunks.text: What makes the tomb special is that its walls still {{show off}} [[colorful]] painted scenes. Time has not {{worn away}} the bright images, which show Paser worshipping the gods inside sacred [[shrines]]. Another painting shows him seated beside his wife, in front of a table piled with [[offerings]]. The art really {{leaps out}} because its colors have [[lasted]] for more than 3,000 years.

chunks.text: The team did not {{come across}} the tomb [[by luck]]. They have worked at this site since 2018, and this season their [[careful]] digging finally {{paid off}}. As they {{cleared away}} sand and fallen stone, a [[courtyard]], a rock chapel, and underground [[burial chambers]] slowly appeared.

chunks.text: News of the find has [[drawn attention]] [[from around the world]]. Officials hope the painted walls will {{shed light on}} Paser's life and his [[exact]] role in Egyptian society. Researchers still need to {{pore over}} the writing on the walls to learn his full [[titles]]. The discovery is [[a reminder of]] how much history still lies buried under Luxor's sands.
